leftEvidence.role: Promise, order, and the approach to the land
leftEvidence.title: Israel is told to leave Horeb and possess the promised land

points.label: Event action and claim
points.left: Moses recalls the command to leave Horeb, enter the Amorite hill country, and possess the land sworn to the ancestors.
points.right: Moses recalls arriving at the Amorite hill country, urging possession without fear, and hearing the people propose men to search the land.

points.label: Response and consequence
points.left: The growing people are organized under selected leaders before Moses resumes the journey account.
points.right: The proposal pleases Moses; twelve men take fruit and report that the land is good.

payload.posture: Deuteronomy first recalls the command to possess the land and later the people’s proposal to send men.

rightEvidence.title: The people propose sending men ahead

payload.tension: The search proposal follows a command already framed by “do not fear.”
payload.title: Commanded departure and the proposal to search
